glosses: zeitlich am Anfang liegend, zum Beginn

examples.text: Nach der sehr langen Feier gingen die Gäste erst am frühen Morgen.
„Früh hatte der Ostgote begonnen, verwandtschaftliche Bande zu anderen Königshäusern zu knüpfen.“

examples.text: Sein früher Tod hat uns alle überrascht.

glosses: in den ersten Morgenstunden, am Morgen

examples.text: Heute früh klingelte es unerwartet an der Tür.
Sehen wir uns Mittwoch früh?
Wissen Sie, ob er morgen früh kommt?
Jeden Tag steht sie morgens früh auf.
„Die Köchin der Frau Grubach, seiner Zimmervermieterin, die ihm jeden Tag gegen acht Uhr früh das Frühstück brachte, kam diesmal nicht.“

glosses: At a time in advance of the usual or expected event.

examples.text: at eleven, we went for an early lunch; she began reading at an early age; his mother suffered an early death

Floods in northern India, mostly in the small state of Uttarakhand, have wrought disaster on an enormous scale. The early, intense onset of the monsoon on June 14th swelled rivers, washing away roads, bridges, hotels and even whole villages. Rock-filled torrents smashed vehicles and homes, burying victims under rubble and sludge.

glosses: Arriving a time before expected; sooner than on time.

examples.text: You're early today! I don't usually see you before nine o'clock.
The early guests sipped their punch and avoided each other's eyes.

glosses: After but close to the start of a period of time.

examples.text: The play "Two Gentlemen of Verona" is one of Shakespeare's early works.
Early results showed their winning 245 out of 300 seats in parliament. The main opponent locked up only 31 seats.

'Twas early June, the new grass was flourishing everywheres, the posies in the yard—peonies and such—in full bloom, the sun was shining, and the water of the bay was blue, with light green streaks where the shoal showed.

Dotcom mania was slow in coming to higher education, but now it has the venerable industry firmly in its grip. Since the launch early last year of Udacity and Coursera, two Silicon Valley start-ups offering free education through MOOCs, massive open online courses, the ivory towers of academia have been shaken to their foundations.
It’s one of the earliest pieces in the comprehensive collection of metronomes by the British instrument dealer Tony Bingham, which forms the bulk of the Basel exhibition.

glosses: In the starting hours of the day.

examples.text: It's too early for this sort of thing. I'm not awake yet.

glosses: Having begun to occur; in its early stages.

examples.text: early cancer

glosses: Of a star or class of stars, hotter than the sun.
A shift (scheduled work period) that takes place early in the day.

examples.text: On my first day on the watch after leaving the shoplifting squad I paraded on earlies but had completely forgotten to take my ear ring off.

glosses: At a time before expected; sooner than usual.

examples.text: We finished the project an hour sooner than scheduled, so we left early.
I had children too early (in life), so my first baby arrived early.

No matter how early I came down, I would find him on the veranda, smoking cigarettes, or otherwise his man would be there with a message to say that his master would shortly join me if I would kindly wait.

While warmer springs cause the early spider orchid to flower earlier in May, climate warming is also causing female bees to emerge from hibernation even earlier – confounding the orchid’s attempts to dupe the male bees.

glosses: Soon; in good time; seasonably.

examples.text: [T]thoſe that ſeeke me early, ſhall find me.

Des pois, des asperges précoces.

examples.text: Un cerisier précoce.

Un abricotier précoce.

glosses: Qualifie un enfant dont l’esprit ou le corps est plus formé que son âge ne le comporte.

examples.text: Mozart était un enfant précoce.
Dès sa plus tendre jeunesse, mon neveu a été un enfant modèle. Il a eu sa première dent à cinq mois et sa première culotte à deux ans. Il a toujours été précoce...

glosses: Qualifie l'esprit d'un tel enfant

examples.text: Un esprit précoce.

glosses: Qualifie ce qui arrive plus tôt qu'habituellement.

examples.text: La lune était toute nouvelle, et, du Nord, le vent apportait l'odeur des précoces jonchées de feuilles à bout de sève, de souches cariées.
Nous avons, cette année, un été précoce.

glosses: Qualifie ce qui se fait plus tôt que le reste.

examples.text: Les sulfatages précoces que beaucoup hésitaient à faire avaient pourtant l'avantage d'atteindre tous les organes de la vigne, notamment les mannes, c'est-à-dire les futurs raisins.

L’herbe à coton, l’élégante linaigrette, semait ses houppes soyeuses, les bourgeons précoces de l’airelle bleue des marais pointaient ça et là. Les prêles dressaient leurs épis bruns au cœur même du tapis de sphaignes.

glosses: Enfant pour lequel on peut parler de précocité intellectuelle.

examples.text: Mais il faut également se méfier des clichés et voir dans chaque enfant original un précoce incompris, ou dans chaque dyslexique, un surdoué méconnu.

glosses: Homme souffrant d'éjaculation précoce.

examples.text: C’est agréable de changer de bord, comme si un homosexuel se faisait prendre par deux blondes hypersexy et beaucoup trop excitantes pour un précoce.
